findings.problem: classify_four returns Vec<&'static str> for a fixed 4-element input, forcing heap allocation on every call for data that is statically bounded to exactly 4 elements.
findings.failure_mode: every call to classify_four allocates a new heap buffer, generates garbage-collection pressure, and defeats cache locality for data that fits in a stack array. The caller pays allocation + deallocation cost for 4 pointers.
findings.fix: return [\&'static str; 4] instead of Vec<\&'static str>. Replace the iterator collect with a fixed array: let mut out: [\&'static str; 4] = ["odd","odd","odd","odd"]; then assign by index. This eliminates all heap allocation for the fixed 4-element case.

findings.problem: The TODO comment asserts Rayon will be faster for a 4-element input without any measurement. Rayon parallel dispatch overhead (thread pool scheduling, work-stealing, result collection) is orders of magnitude larger than the cost of iterating 4 bytes sequentially.
findings.failure_mode: if a developer follows this TODO and introduces Rayon, every call will spawn or borrow from a thread pool, adding microseconds of scheduling overhead per call. For 4 elements this is measurably slower than sequential iteration by a wide margin.
findings.fix: remove the Rayon suggestion entirely. If parallelism is ever needed, benchmark with a workload of millions of elements first. For 4-element inputs, sequential iteration or a fixed array is the only correct choice.

findings.problem: The TODO comment asserts SmallVec will be faster. SmallVec has inline-capacity management and fallback-allocation path overhead that is unnecessary when the output size is statically known to be 4. A fixed array has zero runtime overhead.
findings.failure_mode: SmallVec still requires a runtime check to decide inline vs heap allocation, adds a drop impl that handles both paths, and for a 4-element result still produces a Drop glue call. A stack array [\&'static str; 4] is zero-overhead.
findings.fix: use [\&'static str; 4] instead of SmallVec. If the output size were variable but small-common-case, SmallVec might be justified with measurement. For fixed 4, it is strictly worse.

findings.problem: The TODO asserts Rayon and SmallVec "will be faster" without workload specification, target hardware, baseline command, baseline measurement, new measurement, variance notes, or regression threshold.
findings.failure_mode: developers follow the folklore suggestion and introduce measurably slower code. The claim is the opposite of truth for tiny fixed inputs, and no measurement exists to justify any performance change.
findings.fix: remove the TODO or replace it with a measured benchmark that shows Rayon/SmallVec beats sequential fixed-array for the actual workload. Until then, the claim is an unverifiable folklore assertion.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for classify_four. The function is the only public API and has no bench target, no Criterion/Bencher code, no perf profiling, no alloc check.
findings.failure_mode: without evidence, there is no way to prove the current implementation is optimal, or that any proposed change (Rayon, SmallVec, fixed array) is actually faster. Performance work without evidence violates the Power-of-Ten performance doctrine.
findings.fix: add a Criterion benchmark for classify_four that measures sequential iteration against a fixed-array return variant, including allocation counts (criterion::plotter) and per-call latency.

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (cargo-flamegraph, perf, or similar) exists to confirm the actual bottleneck is here or that optimization is needed at all.
findings.failure_mode: optimizing an unmeasured hot path wastes engineering effort on cold code. The function may never execute in the critical path.
findings.fix: run profiler against the actual workload to confirm classify_four is in a hot path before optimizing.

findings.problem: No allocation tracking evidence (e.g., dyon, jemalloc profiling, or Criterion allocation measurement) exists to quantify the cost of the Vec allocation per call.
findings.failure_mode: cannot quantify the allocation cost to compare against fixed-array baseline. The economic case for fixing the allocation is unproven.
findings.fix: run allocation benchmark to measure bytes/allocation per call for current Vec return vs fixed array.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for classify_four or any proposed optimization
no profiler evidence that classify_four is in a hot path
no allocation measurement comparing Vec<\&'static str> vs [\&'static str; 4]
no second-ring evidence for Rayon or SmallVec folklore claims
no baseline measurement of current implementation latency or throughput
residual_risk: The function is currently safe and correct but allocates unnecessarily on every call for a fixed-size output. The folklore TODO about Rayon and SmallVec is an active risk: a developer following it would introduce measurably slower code. Without benchmarks, there is no evidence that any change would improve performance. The simplest safe fix is [\&'static str; 4] return type which eliminates all allocation for the 4-element fixed case.
